title: Export shipping assurance runbook - Splunk/Datadog/Sentinel
content:
Purpose:
This runbook defines operational acceptance criteria, mapping guidance, and a lightweight checklist for shipping SIEM exports to Splunk, Datadog, and Microsoft Sentinel. It focuses on three cross-cutting concerns: RBAC v2 compatibility and mapping; consistent audit-log schema and required evidence fields; and evidence automation hooks & connector behavior under load.

Audience:
Engineering owners (connector team), security compliance, solutions engineering, and customer onboarding leads. Intended for use during partner/cust connector validation, onboarding calls, and post-deploy incident drills.

High-level goals (pass/fail criteria):
- Connector must deliver audit events that contain the minimum evidence contract (see section: Minimum evidence schema).
- Role and tenant metadata must be preserved and mappable to customer SIEM RBAC constructs (RBAC v2 -> destination mapping).
- Export throughput and backpressure behavior must be demonstrated with a customer-sized workload (load test report attached as linked artifact).
- Evidence automation hooks (idempotent markers, proof-of-delivery fields) must be present for legal/compliance auditability.
- Failover mode: when primary export fails, the connector must not drop PII fields silently and must enter a degraded-safe mode (buffer + encrypt + retry).

Minimum evidence schema (required fields):
- event_id (string, stable UUID)
- timestamp_utc (ISO8601)
- tenant_id (string)
- principal_id (string) - map from RBAC v2 subject
- principal_role (string) - RBAC v2 role (e.g., admin, reader, auditor, integrator)
- action (string) - canonical verb (create/read/update/delete/authz_check/login, etc.)
- object_type (string) - e.g., route, model, deployment, secret, config
- object_id (string) - opaque id or path
- outcome (string) - success|failure|partial
- request_context (string) - short context (route, api_path)
- client_ip (string) - optional but recommended
- correlation_id (string) - request-scoped, used for evidence automation

Optional but strongly recommended fields:
- token_cost (number as string) - for chargeable events
- model_variant (string)
- quantization_profile (string)
- kv_cache_hit (true|false as string)

Envelope patterns by destination (examples):
- Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC):  post to /services/collector with index metadata and event payload. Provide index and sourcetype in headers. Example event payload (stringified JSON) must contain the minimum evidence schema under event.
- Datadog Logs Intake: submit with ddsource=redwood-inference and service set to the feature area. Use tags for tenant_id and region.
- Sentinel: use Azure Monitor Data Collector API pattern with custom log name: RedwoodAudit_CL. Flatten object fields to strings to satisfy Kusto ingestion rules.

RBAC v2 -> SIEM mapping guidance:
- RBAC v2 defines principals with roles, resource scoping (tenant, org, project), and grant timestamps. For export: always send both principal_id and principal_role. When a role is compound (team+role), send principal_role as compound string but include role_components tag in tags array (e.g., ["team:billing","role:auditor"]).
- For customers wanting rolestore integration (mapping to their SIEM roles), provide an optional field mapped_role that solutions engineers can populate during onboarding. This is not required by default.

Evidence automation hooks (contract):
- Each exported event must include correlation_id and event_id. Evidence automation systems will poll/consume events and mark them as present in the evidence ledger once a valid event with those ids arrives.
- Idempotency: event_id must be stable for retries; repeated deliveries with same event_id should be treated as duplicates by downstream connectors.
- Proof-of-delivery fields (added by exporter): delivery_attempts, last_delivery_status, last_delivery_timestamp. These fields are appended by connector for observability and can be included in a companion metadata index.

Connector runtime behavior checklist (pre-onboarding, must be run by connector owner):
- [ ] Schema validation implemented (reject events missing required keys).
- [ ] Backpressure strategy documented (drop oldest/youngest, buffer size, disk persist, retry windows).
- [ ] TLS and certificate pinning validated for HEC/Datadog/Sentinel endpoints.
- [ ] RBAC metadata forwarded and not redacted by default.
- [ ] PII redaction policy applied per-customer configuration (not by default).
- [ ] Rate limit handling: map destination 429s to internal retry with jitter.
- [ ] Batch sizing heuristics (max bytes, max records, max latency) exposed as runtime knobs.
- [ ] Test harness attached: replay harness for customer-provided sample traces.

Operational run scenarios (runbook steps):
A. Onboarding smoke test (30 minutes)
1. Solutions eng and customer agree on sample tenant_id and test principal.
2. Activate connector in test mode, route to customer test HEC/Datadog/Sentinel endpoint.
3. Use replay harness to send 1k representative events across load/policy patterns.
4. Verify 100% of events land in target index within SLA (5 minutes for smoke).
5. Verify event schema, keyed fields, and that event_id/correlation_id are present.
6. Confirm RBAC role mapping matches expectation.
7. Sign-off: capture screenshot of target SIEM query results and attach to onboarding ticket.

B. Degraded export (destination outage)
1. Connector sees consistent 5xx responses or connection failures for >30s.
2. Connector switches to encrypted disk-backed buffer and marks outputs as pending.
3. Send alert to oncall with buffer utilization metrics.
4. Expose temporary degraded telemetry to customer (via status webhook) and include earliest event timestamp pending.
5. When destination is available, replay from oldest-first with preserved event_ids.

C. Evidence preservation audit (quarterly)
1. Run evidence ingestion job to re-index last 90 days of exported events into a compliance ledger (S3 + manifest).
2. Verify sample of events by correlation_id against internal request traces.
3. Flag any missing events and run recovery drill using persisted connector buffers.

Sample envelope examples (flattened strings where necessary):
- Splunk (HEC) event example:
{
  "time": "2026-02-18T21:02:13Z",
  "host": "redwood-prod-connector-1",
  "index": "customer-abc-audit",
  "sourcetype": "redwood:audit:event",
  "event": {
    "event_id": "c6b2f7a2-8e44-4b1f-9c4b-7d53a6f61d3a",
    "timestamp_utc": "2026-02-18T21:02:12Z",
    "tenant_id": "cust-abc",
    "principal_id": "u_4721",
    "principal_role": "billing:auditor",
    "action": "read",
    "object_type": "deployment",
    "object_id": "deploy-39f",
    "outcome": "success",
    "request_context": "/v1/deployments/get",
    "correlation_id": "corr-9932",
    "client_ip": "198.51.100.25"
  }
}

- Datadog example (log payload):
{
  "ddsource": "redwood-inference",
  "service": "redwood-audit",
  "host": "connector-2",
  "message": "audit event",
  "attributes": {
    "tenant_id": "cust-abc",
    "event_id": "c6b2f7a2-8e44-4b1f-9c4b-7d53a6f61d3a",
    "principal_id": "u_4721",
    "action": "authz_check",
    "outcome": "failure",
    "correlation_id": "corr-9932"
  }
}

- Sentinel (Kusto-friendly flattened example):
RedwoodAudit_CL | event_id:string | timestamp_utc:string | tenant_id:string | principal_id:string | principal_role:string | action:string | object_type:string | object_id:string | outcome:string | correlation_id:string
values: ("c6b2f7a2-8e44-4b1f-9c4b-7d53a6f61d3a","2026-02-18T21:02:12Z","cust-abc","u_4721","billing:auditor","read","deployment","deploy-39f","success","corr-9932")

Throttling, retries and SLO mapping recommendations:
- Map destination 429s to exponential backoff with cap at 30s between attempts.
- Maintain a queue depth alert at 70% of buffer size and an error-rate alert at >1% failed deliveries per 1h window.
- For high-volume customers (>=1M events/day), recommend batching by tenant and using a dedicated index/ingestion API key per-tenant to ease downstream filtering and retention.

Privacy & PII handling:
- Default behavior: do not redact tenant_id, principal_id, or object_id. Redaction is configurable per-customer during onboarding and must be recorded in the customer contract.
- Sensitive fields that may contain freeform text (request_context, metadata blobs) must be run through a deterministic redaction pipeline if the customer requests. Keep a redaction log manifest for audits.

Testing matrix (minimum required tests):
- Unit: schema validation, idempotency, header formation (x-splunk-...), dd-api-key header, azure auth token rotation.
- Integration: end-to-end delivery to a test HEC, Datadog staging, and Sentinel workspace.
- Load: 99th percentile latency for export path under 95th percentile traffic must be <500ms (post-batching).
- Recovery: restore from disk-backed buffer within 10 minutes of destination recovery, no event duplication beyond duplicate-event-id checks.

Onboarding artifacts to capture (attach to ticket):
- Customer sample events (sanitized)
- Target ingestion endpoint, index/log name, and API key rotation policy
- Agreed retention and redaction policy (contract clause id)
- Test harness runbook and pass/fail screenshots

Open issues & follow-ups (owner assignments):
- Add automated Kusto schema generator for Sentinel (owner: Rina Shah) - JIRA-SEC-2045
- Include model_variant as a formal telemetry field for token-level cost disputes (owner: Product API)
- (Research) Evaluate compact binary envelope for high-throughput customers to reduce bandwidth (owner: Applied ML infra)

Appendix A: Quick troubleshooting commands
- Splunk search to validate events by correlation_id: index=customer-abc-audit sourcetype=redwood:audit:event correlation_id=corr-9932 | table _time, event.event_id, event.principal_id, event.action, event.outcome
- Datadog logs query: source:redwood-inference @attributes.correlation_id:corr-9932 | sort @timestamp desc | limit 50
- Sentinel Kusto query: RedwoodAudit_CL | where correlation_id == "corr-9932" | project timestamp_utc, event_id, principal_id, action, outcome

Appendix B: Example onboarding checklist (to be completed by Solutions Eng):
- [ ] Verify destination credentials and least-privilege API key
- [ ] Confirm index/log name and retention policy
- [ ] Agree redaction policy and sign contract clause (if non-default)
- [ ] Run smoke test and attach evidence to ticket
- [ ] Schedule go/no-go with customer security team

Notes:
- This document is intentionally prescriptive but lightweight: we prefer explicit minimal evidence fields over large, inconsistent freeform payloads. If customers need additional fields, create a short addendum per-customer.
- For legal or audits, preservation of event_id + correlation_id + timestamp is the minimal contract we will accept.

End of runbook.
